summary: The committed-versus-working-tree discipline is exactly right and I verified every part of it: the HEAD blob hashes to 2cbad561, the working-tree file to 2d95f22c, and my own review file records 2cbad561 at both start and end with ACCEPT at 0 blockers, so the dual ACCEPT really is of the bytes being recorded. Both replacement targets are verbatim and unique. But the DR-105 half asserts that a permission v2 successor remains owed, and adopted D-042 records permission-truth-tables.v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate at a digest I confirmed on disk, with dual 0-blocker verdicts and no supersession. The entry would write that contradiction into file 08 dated today, in the row D-042 governs, while mentioning neither D-042 nor v2 anywhere in its replacement text.

objections.claim: The entry states, and would write into file 08 dated 2026-08-14, that a permission v2 successor is still owed for DR-105. Adopted D-042 records permission-truth-tables.v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate.
objections.why: D-042 is titled 'Record permission-truth-tables.v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate', is ADOPTED 2026-08-13 with CONSENT from both reviewers at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, pins the subject at cce3afcaee90bbca388825a474751d6ebb17b30722b35dadcf6c631b34a8731a, and records dual ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers. I confirmed the artifact exists on disk at exactly that digest, and I checked for supersession before calling this — every later mention of D-042 in COORD is a 'same form as D-035 / D-038 / D-042' citation, none of them touching its standing. So v2 is not owed; it landed eight days before this draft. Three things make the misstatement consequential rather than cosmetic. First, this is an MF-6 register write, so the claim does not merely sit in a draft — it is inscribed into the authoritative row as current status with today's date. Second, the replacement is the only update D-093 makes to DR-105's status cell and it mentions neither D-042 nor v2; I verified that mechanically across all four fenced blocks. A reader of the resulting cell would take DR-105's design-contract position to be permission-truth-tables.v1 at REJECT with a successor still awaited, when the row in fact holds an independently accepted v2. Third, it is self-undermining in an entry of this class: D-093 exists to record that an independently accepted candidate exists for a row, and in the same clause it denies that a different independently accepted candidate exists for the same row. There is a related fact that explains how this arose but does not excuse it: file 08 has never recorded D-042 at all — zero mentions of either 'D-042' or 'permission-truth-tables.v2' — because D-042's clause 4 says 'Does not edit file 08'. The live DR-105 cell therefore still carries the pre-D-042 sentence 'a permission v2 successor and the host-effect contract remain'. That staleness is inherited. What this entry does is restate the stale half as current in new words under a new date, which converts inherited staleness into an affirmative new misstatement — the D-092 pattern escalated, since there the stale text was merely left standing.
objections.repair: Strike 'a permission v2 successor' from clause 3 and from the DR-105 replacement, and record D-042's v2 as DR-105's accepted design-contract candidate alongside the host-effect candidate this entry records. If what is actually owed is a successor to v2 carrying D-042's advisories P2-01, P2-02, P2-03 and PT2-CX-A1, say that in those terms, since the current phrasing reads as the pre-D-042 claim it reproduces.

notesNonBlocking.observation: After adoption the register will pin the path at its committed digest 2cbad561… while the file at that path on disk hashes 2d95f22c…, and its review prompt is likewise modified. Anyone verifying the pin by hashing the working-tree path — the ordinary reflex in this corpus, and the one I have used on every other pinned artifact this session — gets a mismatch and no explanation from the register. The entry handles this correctly for its own purposes by naming the retrieval command explicitly, and it is right not to record bytes that carry no ACCEPT. But the divergence outlives the decision. Resolving the working-tree state, by reverting the mutation or by putting it through its own review cycle, would remove a standing trap; failing that, the recorded cell could carry the 'git show HEAD:' qualifier the draft uses, so the mismatch is self-explaining at the point of use.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with one MUST-FIX. The part of this entry that looked hardest is the part that holds: distinguishing a committed blob from a working-tree mutation of the same path is exactly the right instinct, and it survives testing from both directions, including the check that actually matters — my own review file records the committed digest as its subject at start and end, so the ACCEPT being cited is an ACCEPT of the bytes being recorded and not of their neighbour. The failure is elsewhere and it is the kind this corpus is built to catch. The entry states that a permission v2 successor is still owed for DR-105, and D-042 recorded permission-truth-tables.v2 as that row's accepted design-contract candidate on 2026-08-13, dual-consented at 0 blockers, with the artifact sitting on disk at the pinned digest and nothing since disturbing it. I checked for supersession before saying so. What makes it a MUST-FIX rather than an inherited-staleness note is that file 08 never recorded D-042 in the first place, so the false clause is not merely being left in place — it is being restated as current, in the row D-042 governs, under today's date, by an entry whose entire purpose is the accurate recording of independently accepted candidates.
